A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SONICS and SpecTTTra. Their main texts, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and reformatted material.

before.justification: v1 reports original SONICS detection experiments, a three-participant human benchmark, computational-efficiency measurements, and dataset analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains original detection, human, and efficiency results and adds SingFake-to-SONICS transfer experiments and qualitative LLM-selection findings.

M1.justification: The spectral and temporal tokenizers, positional embeddings, transformer encoder, pooling, classifier, and three patch-size variants remain unchanged. The generation pipelines and appendix tokenizer code are also retained. Newly documented augmentation and filtering details do not establish a redesign of the proposed method.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates detectors on SONICS alone. v3 Table 2 adds training and evaluation on SingFake and transfer to SONICS, extending coverage from end-to-end synthetic songs to the distinct singing-voice-deepfake domain and cross-dataset generalization. SONICS membership and its existing split counts remain unchanged.

E2.justification: v3 adds EfficientViT-B2 to the AI, human-AI, and efficiency comparisons alongside the retained ConvNeXt and ViT baselines. This adds a relevant efficient hybrid architecture without replacing the existing comparator set.

E3.justification: The added SingFake experiment uses 597 training and 480 test/validation songs, ImageNet initialization, resized 224×224 spectrograms, and EER alongside the other metrics. Existing SONICS splits and testing procedures are retained. The reported efficiency memory batch changes from 14 to 12 in the main text, but v3 Appendix B still specifies 14, leaving the actual setting unresolved.

E4.justification: The new transfer experiment tests whether SingFake-trained detectors generalize to end-to-end synthetic songs. Appendix D also adds qualitative comparisons of LLMs for lyrics generation and song-style analysis. Existing duration, embedding-space, and long-context illustrations are retained; no new component ablation is reported.

E5.justification: v3 Appendix B first specifies five warm-up runs followed by 100 timing runs, with processing times averaged before computing speed. This discloses repeated measurement and averaging, rather than establishing an increase in repetitions. Neither version reports training-seed variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Between v1 Table 3 and v3 Table 4, reported 120-second F1 changes from 0.94 to 0.97 for SpecTTTra-α and from 0.91 to 0.88 for γ; ConvNeXt remains 0.96, changing the leading model. v3 adds EfficientViT results and transfer findings, including ConvNeXt F1 of 0.86 on SingFake versus 0.33 on SONICS. Efficiency values also change, but differing or conflicting batch settings preclude interpreting lower memory figures as same-setting improvements.

T1.justification: v3 removes v1's erroneous assertion of an exponential computational-cost increase while retaining the quadratic attention-scaling explanation. This is a limited correction to complexity reasoning. Equations 1–3 remain mathematically equivalent, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The dataset, long-context modeling, and benchmarking contributions remain. The model-performance claim strengthens: v1 emphasizes competitive accuracy with efficiency, whereas v3's abstract claims that its best variant exceeds ViT by eight F1 percentage points and ConvNeXt by one while also being faster and using less memory.

C2.justification: v3 revises the accuracy-efficiency interpretation around α's new leading result and discusses EfficientViT's resource costs. It links existing label smoothing to retrieval noise and adds limitations concerning small model sizes and absent audio pretraining. Conversely, it removes v1's explicit English-only limitation and real-song copyright/access discussion.

D1.justification: v3 substantially expands documentation with generation/download APIs, PyAnnote vocal filtering, augmentation parameters, explicit transformer dimensions, timing procedures, and FLOP tooling. It also discloses the 600-song retrieval audit and adds models to the promised resource release. However, v1's training batch size of 128, learning rate of 0.0005, and real-song download guidance disappear. The PDFs do not establish that newly documented processing steps were newly introduced.

R1.justification: v3 adds discussion of Singing Voice Graph Modeling and EfficientViT, plus references supporting Qwen-Audio, augmentation, optimization, and implementation tools. The Ytmdl reference is removed. The principal positioning against existing SVDD datasets and long-audio approaches remains intact.

P1.justification: v3 polishes and expands passages throughout the abstract, model explanation, results, limitations, and appendices, and reorders parts of the fake-song generation description. The main section framework, appendix organization, and substantial portions of the explanatory and prompt text remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 adds the transfer-results table and combines v1's separate training/test and validation summaries into Table 3. Benchmark tables are regrouped, token-count equations are boxed, and Figures 3–4 receive notation and styling refinements. Captions are expanded, while the generation diagrams, dataset plots, and interface screenshots are retained.

improvement.justification: The new transfer experiment supplies direct evidence for the claimed gap between SVDD and end-to-end song detection, while EfficientViT broadens the efficiency comparison and the expanded appendix improves implementation transparency. These are useful gains beyond higher reported scores. Their benefit is limited by omitted training hyperparameters and the conflicting memory-benchmark batch sizes of 12 and 14, supporting a modest overall improvement.
